relationships.description: If the threat is realized, the attacker would read or modify the protected resource, such as dumping rows from a customer database or altering records through an API.
relationships.evidence: The threat-model entry's STRIDE category (information disclosure or tampering) names the specific API, database or file whose contents the attack would read or change.

relationships.description: The threat entry collects the countermeasures recorded against it as its mitigation set, and each control can also exist on its own and be shared with other threats.
relationships.evidence: The threat-model document or risk register lists countermeasure IDs under the threat's mitigations section, and the same control IDs appear under other threats.

relationships.description: The threat justifies a restrictive access predicate, such as requiring an MFA claim or a trusted IP range, that narrows when requests are allowed.
relationships.evidence: The access condition's rationale field or the policy source comment cites the threat ID as the reason the attribute check exists.

relationships.description: The threat's likelihood and impact inform the classification tier assigned to data and the minimum protection obligations, such as encryption, attached to that tier.
relationships.evidence: The data classification standard cites the threat's risk rating as justification for the tier's handling rules, for example mandatory encryption at rest.

relationships.description: The threat shapes which rules a security policy contains and how it is prioritized, so that access decisions for the affected target category counter the attack.
relationships.evidence: The policy definition file, its change record or the threat model's linked-controls column references the threat ID as the driver of specific rules or of the policy's priority.

relationships.description: The threat is traced to the security requirement that states the verifiable 'shall' property the system must meet so that the threat is addressed.
relationships.evidence: A requirements traceability matrix row or requirement metadata links the requirement ID to the threat ID it was derived from.

relationships.description: The documented threat is a concrete instance of the security-risk condition named by the driver, for example 'rising credential-theft attacks', that prompts the organization to set security goals.
relationships.evidence: The driver's description in the motivation model cites specific threat-model entries as the evidence that substantiates the condition.

relationships.description: The attack is aimed at disrupting, abusing or defrauding the business process, such as invoice fraud inserted into a payment-approval process.
relationships.evidence: The threat entry's affected-asset or impact field names the business process, or the process documentation lists the threat in its risk section.

relationships.description: The attack is aimed at degrading or compromising the externally offered business service, such as a denial-of-service attack against Order Delivery.
relationships.evidence: The threat's impact statement or business impact assessment names the business service whose availability or integrity would be lost.

relationships.description: The attack seeks to disclose, tamper with or destroy that category of information, such as exfiltration of payment card data.
relationships.evidence: The threat-model entry's asset field or data-flow diagram annotation identifies the information category, for example PII or cardholder data, as what the attacker is after.

relationships.description: The protected resource is the attack surface the threat is directed at, such as a SQL injection against a customer-search API.
relationships.evidence: The threat-model data-flow diagram element or the threat's target field names the specific API, database, file or UI area.

relationships.description: Identifying the threat prompts an audit configuration that records the security events indicating the attack, such as logging failed logins to detect credential stuffing.
relationships.evidence: The audit configuration's event list or a detection requirement is annotated with the threat ID whose indicators it captures.

notes: accesses secureresource duplicates targets secureresource. aggregates countermeasure inverts the natural 'countermeasure mitigates threat' and is not whole-part. maps-to is a data-schema predicate misused for traceability. realizes driver is semantically wrong; influence or associated-with fits better. triggers auditconfig and constrains accesscondition describe design motivation, not runtime triggering or constraint; influence fits better.
